name: Cochrane
description: Global, independent network of researchers, professionals, and patients that prepares and maintains Cochrane systematic reviews of health care evidence.

name: Centre for Reviews and Dissemination (CRD)
description: University of York research centre producing evidence syntheses for health and social care policy, and host of the PROSPERO register of review protocols.

name: Risk of Bias Tools (RoB 2 and ROBINS-I)
description: Official home of the Cochrane RoB 2 tool for randomised trials and the ROBINS-I tool for non-randomised studies, with detailed guidance and downloadable templates.

name: GRADEpro GDT
description: Web application for creating GRADE evidence profiles and Summary of Findings tables, developed in cooperation with the GRADE Working Group.

name: AMSTAR
description: Home of the AMSTAR and AMSTAR 2 instruments for critically appraising the methodological quality of systematic reviews of health care interventions.

name: PEDro, the Physiotherapy Evidence Database
description: Database of randomised controlled trials, systematic reviews, and practice guidelines in physiotherapy, with PEDro ratings of trial methodological quality.
publisher: Institute for Musculoskeletal Health, University of Sydney

name: AHRQ Effective Health Care Program
description: US program that commissions and publishes evidence reports and systematic reviews comparing treatments, tests, and health care interventions for clinical decisions.
publisher: Agency for Healthcare Research and Quality

name: Evidence Aid
description: Charity that curates and summarizes evidence from systematic reviews to support disaster preparedness, response, and humanitarian health decisions.

name: Health Systems Evidence
description: Database of evidence syntheses, policy briefs, and governance documents supporting health system strengthening and health policy decision making.

name: Cochrane Crowd
description: Cochrane's citizen science community where volunteers classify study records to help identify trials and support evidence synthesis tasks.

name: Cochrane Learning Hub
description: Cochrane's learning hub with free introductory training on evidence and systematic reviews, including the Evidence Essentials interactive course.

name: AGREE Trust
description: Home of the AGREE II instrument and related resources for appraising the quality and reporting of clinical practice guidelines.

name: BMC Medical Research Methodology
description: Open-access journal publishing research on methods used in medical research, including study design, systematic review methodology, and data collection.

name: Systematic Reviews
description: Open-access journal publishing protocols, methods research, and completed systematic reviews and meta-analyses across health and social sciences.

name: DistillerSR
description: Commercial platform for managing systematic review projects, covering protocol design, literature screening, data extraction, and quality control.

name: International Council for Harmonisation (ICH)
description: International body harmonizing technical requirements for medicines, publisher of the ICH E6 Good Clinical Practice guideline central to trial ethics and quality.

name: Health Research Authority (HRA)
description: UK regulator that approves and oversees health and social care research, coordinating Research Ethics Committee review and research governance policy.

name: Finnish National Board on Research Integrity (TENK)
description: Finnish national expert body on research integrity and the ethical review of human sciences research, publisher of the Finnish code of conduct for researchers.
publisher: Finnish National Board on Research Integrity

name: Norwegian National Research Ethics Committees (NESH)
description: Umbrella body for the Norwegian National Research Ethics Committees, publishing guidelines on research ethics, integrity, and internet research across disciplines.

name: Panel on Research Ethics (Government of Canada)
description: Canadian Panel on Research Ethics, steward of the Tri-Council Policy Statement TCPS 2 governing ethical conduct for research involving humans in Canada.

name: National Health and Medical Research Council (NHMRC)
description: Australian government agency issuing the National Statement on Ethical Conduct in Human Research along with research integrity and animal ethics guidance.
publisher: National Health and Medical Research Council

name: The Hastings Center
description: Independent bioethics research institute addressing ethical questions in medicine, science, technology, and the life sciences through scholarship and public engagement.

name: Nuffield Council on Bioethics
description: UK body that examines and advises on ethical questions raised by biological and medical research, publishing independent reports and policy briefings.

name: AAHRPP
description: Accreditation body for human research protection programs, setting standards and accrediting IRBs, universities, hospitals, and research organizations worldwide.

name: Public Responsibility in Medicine and Research (PRIM&R)
description: Professional community providing education, conferences, and resources on research ethics, IRB practice, and human subjects protections.

name: CITI Program
description: Widely used training platform offering certified courses in human subjects research, responsible conduct of research, animal care, and data privacy.

name: European Data Protection Board (EDPB)
description: Independent EU body ensuring consistent application of the GDPR, issuing guidelines relevant to research data protection and international data transfers.

name: Council of Science Editors (CSE)
description: Professional association of science editors, publisher of the CSE style manual and the white paper on promoting integrity in scientific journal publishing.

name: AAALAC International
description: Private nonprofit that accredits animal care and use programs in research, testing, and education, promoting humane and ethical laboratory animal science.

name: NIH Office of Laboratory Animal Welfare (OLAW)
description: NIH office administering the Public Health Service Policy on Humane Care and Use of Laboratory Animals and overseeing institutional assurances for animal research.

name: Centre for Evidence-Based Medicine (CEBM), University of Oxford
description: Oxford centre teaching and researching evidence-based medicine, with toolkits for critical appraisal, study design, and EBM teaching resources.

name: Berkeley Initiative for Transparency in the Social Sciences (BITSS)
description: UC Berkeley initiative promoting research transparency in economics and the social sciences, running training on preanalysis plans and replicable methods.

name: RECORD Statement
description: RECORD guideline, an extension of STROBE for reporting studies conducted using routinely collected health data, with checklist and explanation documents.

name: SQUIRE Statement
description: SQUIRE guidelines for reporting quality improvement studies in health care, providing checklist items and explanatory material for authors and reviewers.

name: STARD Statement
description: STARD standards for reporting diagnostic accuracy studies, with checklists and flow diagrams for studies comparing diagnostic tests against reference standards.

name: National Centre for Research Methods (NCRM)
description: UK centre providing training and resources across social science research methods, from survey design to qualitative, comparative, and digital methods.

name: IASSIST
description: International association of data professionals supporting social science research through data services, curation practice, and the IASSIST Quarterly journal.
publisher: International Association for Social Science Information Services and Technology

name: AsPredicted
description: Preregistration service where researchers answer structured questions to create a time-stamped, citable preregistration document for their studies.

name: Digital Curation Centre (DCC)
description: UK centre of expertise in digital curation, best known for the DMPonline data management planning tool and the digital curation lifecycle model.

name: Research Data Alliance (RDA)
description: Community organization building social and technical infrastructure for open data sharing through international working groups and interest groups.

name: Meta-Research Innovation Center at Stanford (METRICS)
description: Stanford center studying research practices and testing interventions that improve the reproducibility and efficiency of biomedical science.

name: Qualitative Data Repository (QDR)
description: Dedicated repository for qualitative and multi-method social science data, curating projects and supporting transparent publication and data citation.

name: Guidelines International Network (G-I-N)
description: International network of guideline-developing organizations sharing guidance documents, methods resources, and a library of clinical practice guidelines.

name: Framework for Open and Reproducible Research Training (FORRT)
description: Community project curating open educational resources, lesson plans, and curricula for teaching open science and reproducible research methods.

name: Peer Community In (PCI)
description: Network of communities in which research preprints receive transparent, open peer review and can be recommended as valid and citable research outputs.

name: International Council for the Exploration of the Sea (ICES)
description: Intergovernmental marine science organization providing peer-reviewed advice on fishing quotas, ecosystem status, and ocean management for the North Atlantic.

name: Climate Change Committee (CCC)
description: Independent UK statutory body advising on emissions targets and climate risk, producing progress reports to Parliament and periodic climate risk assessments.

name: National Toxicology Program (NTP)
description: US interagency program that tests chemicals and publishes toxicology studies, including the Report on Carcinogens identifying substances that may cause cancer.
publisher: National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences

name: International Agency for Research on Cancer (IARC)
description: WHO cancer agency running the IARC Monographs program that classifies environmental exposures, occupations, and habits as causes of human cancer.

name: Global Carbon Project
description: International research project publishing the annual Global Carbon Budget, quantifying fossil fuel emissions, land use fluxes, and atmospheric carbon sinks.

name: International Resource Panel
description: UNEP-hosted science panel assessing the sustainable use of natural resources, publishing the Global Resources Outlook and material flow assessments.

name: The Economics of Ecosystems and Biodiversity (TEEB)
description: UNEP-hosted initiative making the economic value of nature visible, with guidance on valuing ecosystem services in policy and business decisions.

name: Agency for Toxic Substances and Disease Registry (ATSDR)
description: US public health agency publishing toxicological profiles for hazardous substances and assessing health risks for communities near contaminated sites.
publisher: Centers for Disease Control and Prevention

name: InterAcademy Partnership (IAP)
description: Global network of national academies of science, engineering, and medicine issuing joint statements and collaborative assessments on science policy topics.

name: PBL Netherlands Environmental Assessment Agency
description: Dutch national agency producing independent environmental assessments and scenario studies for Dutch, European, and global policy questions.

name: Lancet Countdown
description: International research collaboration tracking the health impacts of climate change and publishing annual indicator reports on climate and health.

name: International Institute for Applied Systems Analysis (IIASA)
description: International research institute producing systems analysis and global scenario assessments on energy, land use, population, and climate.

name: European Commission Joint Research Centre (JRC)
description: European Commission science service providing independent evidence and assessments for EU policy on environment, energy, food security, and safety.

name: Environmental Performance Index (EPI)
description: Biennial index from Yale and Columbia universities ranking countries on environmental health and ecosystem vitality using published performance indicators.
publisher: Yale Center for Environmental Law and Policy

name: Binder (MyBinder)
description: Free public service that turns GitHub repositories into live, executable computing environments for reproducible notebooks and code.

name: Whole Tale
description: NSF-funded platform for creating and publishing reproducible computational narratives that bundle code, data, and execution environments together.

name: ReproZip
description: Open-source tool that traces executed research workflows and packs files, dependencies, and environment details into a reproducible bundle.

name: The Turing Way
description: Community handbook on data science practices for reproducible, ethical, and collaborative research, covering version control, testing, and reproducibility.

name: Project Jupyter
description: Open-source ecosystem of interactive computing tools, including Jupyter Notebook and JupyterLab, widely used for reproducible data analysis and teaching.

name: Quarto
description: Open-source publishing system for reproducible documents that renders notebooks and code in Python, R, Julia, and Observable to many output formats.

name: Figshare
description: Repository where researchers publish figures, datasets, media, and papers with DOIs and flexible licensing, including institution-hosted instances.

name: Dryad
description: Open repository for research data across disciplines, with journal-integrated curation and licensing of accepted datasets under CC0 for reuse.

name: UK Reproducibility Network (UKRN)
description: National consortium of UK universities advancing reproducible research through institutional leads, training, and research on research practices.

name: NumFOCUS
description: Nonprofit that sponsors core open-source scientific computing projects including NumPy, pandas, Matplotlib, and Jupyter, supporting sustainable research software.

name: R Consortium
description: Industry consortium within the Linux Foundation supporting the R computing community through infrastructure, working groups, and project funding.

name: The Carpentries
description: Global community teaching foundational coding and data skills to researchers through peer-led Software, Data, and Library Carpentry workshops.

name: SORTEE
description: Society for Open, Reliable, and Transparent Ecology and Evolutionary Biology, promoting open and reproducible research practices through events and resources.

name: DataLad
description: Open-source command line tool for managing, versioning, and sharing data alongside code, built on git-annex for large scientific datasets.

name: Software Sustainability Institute (SSI)
description: UK institute helping researchers build better software, with fellowship programs, policy work, and guidance on sustainable research software practices.

name: Institute for Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME)
description: Research center at the University of Washington producing the Global Burden of Disease study, population health estimates, and health system performance assessments.

name: WorldPop
description: University of Southampton program producing high-resolution open gridded population estimates, age and sex structure rasters, and demographic projections.

name: SEDAC, the Socioeconomic Data and Applications Center
description: NASA data center at Columbia University focused on human interactions with the environment, with population, poverty, climate exposure, and infrastructure datasets.

name: Survey of Health, Ageing and Retirement in Europe (SHARE)
description: Cross-national longitudinal survey of health, ageing, and retirement providing harmonized microdata from households across Europe and Israel.

name: Health and Retirement Study (HRS)
description: Longitudinal US survey of Americans over age 50 providing harmonized data on health, employment, income, and family for aging research.

name: English Longitudinal Study of Ageing (ELSA)
description: Longitudinal study of a representative sample of people aged 50 and over in England, covering health, economic circumstances, and social participation.

name: Gateway to Global Aging Data
description: Harmonized data platform for aging surveys worldwide, crosswalking HRS family studies such as ELSA, SHARE, and CHARLS for cross-national research.

name: Panel Study of Income Dynamics (PSID)
description: Longest running US household panel survey, tracking families since 1968 with data on income, employment, wealth, health, and intergenerational dynamics.

name: Population Association of America (PAA)
description: Professional association for demographic and population research, hosting the annual PAA meeting and supporting the field through advocacy and awards.

name: International Union for the Scientific Study of Population (IUSSP)
description: International professional association promoting population research worldwide, with scientific panels, conferences, and policy engagement resources.

name: International Organization for Migration (IOM)
description: UN migration agency publishing global migration statistics, migrant flow data, and the World Migration Report series for researchers and policymakers.

name: Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre (IDMC)
description: Geneva-based centre monitoring internal displacement worldwide, publishing conflict and disaster displacement estimates and the annual Global Report.

name: Integrated Postsecondary Education Data System (IPEDS)
description: US federal system collecting annual data from every college and university, covering enrollments, completions, finance, and institutional characteristics.

name: College Scorecard
description: US Department of Education tool publishing data on college costs, graduation rates, and post-enrollment earnings for students and researchers.

name: National Student Clearinghouse
description: Nonprofit clearinghouse tracking enrollment and degree records for most US higher education students, publishing research reports on pathways and outcomes.

name: Education Endowment Foundation (EEF)
description: UK charity funding evaluations of teaching interventions and publishing the Teaching and Learning Toolkit with evidence on what works in schools.

name: CLOSER
description: Consortium of UK longitudinal studies harmonizing metadata and training researchers to use cohort studies spanning birth through adulthood.

name: UK Data Archive
description: Largest UK archive of social science and economic data, curating and preserving survey, qualitative, and administrative datasets for reuse.

name: Global Partnership for Education (GPE)
description: Global fund and partnership supporting education systems in lower-income countries, publishing data and analysis on education financing and access.

name: Global Education Monitoring (GEM) Report
description: UNESCO program publishing the annual Global Education Monitoring Report with world education data, inclusion analysis, and policy recommendations.

name: American Educational Research Association (AERA)
description: Major professional society for education research, publishing peer-reviewed journals and hosting one of the largest annual education research meetings.

name: Social Science Research Council (SSRC)
description: Independent council mobilizing social science for public knowledge through fellowship programs, working groups, and interdisciplinary research platforms.

name: Institute of Education Sciences (IES)
description: Independent US education statistics and research agency funding rigorous studies, evidence clearinghouses, and regional education laboratories.

name: American Institutes for Research (AIR)
description: Nonprofit behavioral and social science research organization conducting evaluations and technical assistance in education, health, and workforce domains.

name: Spencer Foundation
description: Private foundation dedicated to funding education research, with grant programs supporting small projects, major studies, and career development awards.

name: Opportunity Insights
description: Harvard-based research lab using large administrative datasets to study economic mobility, publishing the Opportunity Atlas and neighborhood-level findings.
